text:
maria: heads-up — after flipping coalesce jitter to 3ms on the canary pool we started seeing a slow drift in p99 for short-context reqs. creating a thread to collect quick datapoints and decide rollback or tweak. :eyes:
zheng: noted. which canary and what config exactly? did we change coalesce delay or just jitter?
maria: canary-3 (eu-west). only changed jitter from 0.5ms -> 3ms, coalesce delay stayed at 6ms. deploy-bot rolled it at 10:22 UTC.
deploy-bot: deployed canary-3 with parameter overrides: {"coalesce_jitter_ms": 3, "coalesce_delay_ms": 6} at 2026-03-18T10:22:12Z :rocket:
perf-bot: quick profile summary (canary-3 vs baseline): p50: 36ms -> 38ms (+5%), p95: 185ms -> 210ms (+13%), p99: 290ms -> 420ms (+45%). GPU util: 62% -> 67%. KV cache miss-rate: 27% -> 42%. Kernel fallback count: +12% to cuda_fallback_v2.
joel: that KV miss jump is huge. coalesce jitter could be affecting request alignment so warm KV entries aren't being reused. are we batching across different conversation keys more often?
zheng: checking kernel-selection logs now — grep shows a correlation between batch composition variance and fallback. when batches include mixed sequence lengths we trigger a different kernel path at generation step ~2-3 tokens for ~12% of samples. suspect jitter increases the window variance so micro-batches are less homogeneous.
alisha: simple repro suggestion: run microbench with jitter=0.5 vs 3. Use same arrival trace and compare batch composition histograms + kernel path counts. I can queue a run on canary infra if someone posts the command.
maria: here's the exact bench command we used on canary: ```
./bench/run_arrival_sim.sh --trace traces/short_context_traffic.json --coalesce-delay-ms 6 --coalesce-jitter-ms 3 --duration 30m --out /tmp/canary3
```
zheng: thx. i'll run local laptop sim first with smaller trace, then spin up 1h canary run. also dumping a small log excerpt that shows the kernel switch (masked): ```
[2026-03-18T10:23:05Z] batch_id=9876 size=4 seq_lens=[16,64,8,20] kernel=optimized_attn_v1 -> fallback=cuda_fallback_v2 at token_idx=2 memory_peak=5.6GB
```
joel: if the batching groups mixed seq lengths more frequently, KV priming won't help because early requests don't warm same KV addresses. caching effectiveness needs similar-key grouping. can we try a queue policy tweak: prefer same-routing-key coalesce (soft affinity) for the first 5ms of window then relax?
alisha: we tried affinity before but it caused throughput regressions for high-slew workloads. maybe make it conditional: affinity when expected batch size < 8 and route-key-hit-rate >= 0.3. small change in policy.
maria: actionable list so far: 1) zheng run bench compare jitter 0.5 vs 3 with same trace + collect batch composition, kernel-path counts, KV hit-rate. 2) joel prototype soft-affinity gate and run quick sim. 3) if repro confirmed, rollback canary to jitter=0.5 and open ops alert.
zheng: started local sim now. ETA 12m for preliminary histograms. posting artifacts when ready. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
perf-bot: FYI instrument hooks to collect per-batch "route_key_entropy" and "seq_len_stddev" were enabled on canary-3 at 10:25 UTC. add --debug-metrics in bench to surface them.
maria: perfect. let's avoid full rollback until zheng posts the histograms unless p99 keeps rising in next 30m. I'll also mute non-critical alerts for canary-3 so we don't wake infra on noise. :thumbsup:
zheng: first-pass results (local sim): jitter=0.5 -> median batch_seq_stddev 8.3, kernel_fallback_rate 3.1%; jitter=3 -> median batch_seq_stddev 21.7, kernel_fallback_rate 15.8%. KV_hit_rate dropped 29% -> 18% in the sim. uploading full traces to /artifacts/canary3/bench_2290123456.tar.gz
joel: those deltas line up with perf-bot numbers. looks like even modest jitter increase can amplify heterogeneity and push more requests down fallback kernels. good find.
alisha: will sketch a soft-affinity patch today. if we can keep batch_seq_stddev < 12 we probably get kernel_fallback back down under 5% and recover p99.
maria: thanks all. keep posts short in this thread with numbers only so we can assemble a short postmortem if we end up rolling back. I'll update the canary channel after next 30m. :wave:
